provider: Alibaba Cloud (Simple Application Server, international site)

free_tier.stated: no free tier on the international site; the smallest Linux plan is USD 3.5 per month for 1 CPU, 0.5 GB RAM, 20 GB SSD

retention.stated: the instance and its disk persist while the subscription is paid; the plan is sold monthly or yearly prepay

egress.terms: 1 TB a month on the USD 4.5 plan, then the excess is billed pay-as-you-go by outbound GB; the page lists Japan (Tokyo) at USD 0.087 per GB

interface_detail: root SSH; the vendor's web console; a REST API where documented
chaining: an English-language Chinese cloud with a Tokyo and Singapore region: the card gate is a real bank card because virtual cards are refused, but there is no passport and no national ID for an overseas region

limits.value: 1 TB a month of data transfer, then pay-as-you-go per GB

binding_note: 4 Mbit/s is about 500 KB/s sustained, so the 1 TB quota is roughly what the port can move in a month anyway; the port is the ceiling, not the quota

identity_cost.detail: email plus a mobile number from outside the Chinese mainland for security verification; real-name verification is required only for resources located in the Chinese mainland or for a credit line, not for an overseas region. A card is bound at signup and 'The system may place a temporary authorization hold on your bank card (only for verification; no money is deducted)'. Virtual credit cards are refused outright: 'the system does not support using virtual credit cards for payment verification or card binding'

confidence_note: price table and the card and identity rules are from first-party Alibaba pages read today

evidence.proved: quoted: '| Price (monthly) | USD 3.5 per month | USD 4.5 per month | USD 9 per month |' with '| RAM | 0.5 GB | 1 GB | 2 GB |', '| SSD | 20 GB | 20 GB | 40 GB |', '| Limited peak bandwidth | 4 Mbit/s | 4 Mbit/s | 6 Mbit/s |' and '| Monthly data transfer | 1 TB | 1 TB | 1.5 TB |'

quoted: 'if the traffic exceeds the upper limit of the package in the current month, the exceeding traffic will be charged at the Pay-As-You-Go rate' and the Tokyo excess rate 'Japan(Tokyo) | USD 0.087 per GB'

quoted: 'Requires an email address for registration, plus a mobile number from outside the Chinese mainland (including Hong Kong (China), Macao (China), and Taiwan (China)) for security verification.' and 'Real-name verification ... Required in specific scenarios ... to purchase or use cloud resources located in the Chinese mainland, or to apply for a credit line.'

quoted: 'The system may place a temporary authorization hold on your bank card (only for verification; no money is deducted).' and 'the system does not support using virtual credit cards for payment verification or card binding'

notes: The 4 Mbit/s port is the worst bandwidth on any qualifying row and the reason the price is low. The yearly prepay price is not on the page read, so the annual figure is unverified. Whether a debit card passes the 'physical bank card' test is not stated.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 4.5 a month, subscription billed monthly; a VPS bills whether it runs or not, so 10 h/day costs the same 4.5

session_cap.note: none; it is a VPS that bills whether it runs or not

extras.english: yes, the whole international site and console
extras.payment_methods: bank card and PayPal; virtual cards refused; temporary authorisation hold, amount not stated
